Here's the program you uploaded — it's Girijananda Chowdhury University (GCU), Assam — M.A./M.Sc. in Psychology.

GCU is a private university in Guwahati, established in 2022. Its School of Humanities and Social Sciences runs the 2-year master's in Psychology with special tracks in clinical, social and neuropsychology. The curriculum was approved by the Board of Studies on 14 Oct 2023.

Quick facts

  • Duration: 2 years (4 semesters)
  • Total credits: 84
    • Discipline Specific Core = 50
    • Discipline Specific Elective (DSE) = 20
    • Internship = 4
    • Dissertation = 4
    • MDC + SEC = 10
  • Fees (2025-26 reports): MA ~ ₹92,000 total; M.Sc. ~ ₹1.1 Lakh tuition
  • Eligibility: bachelor's degree (generally 45–55% in relevant subject)

What you’ll study

Semester 1 – 22 credits

  • Emergence of Psychology (4)
  • Psychological Processes I (4)
  • Research Methodology I (4)
  • Personality and Self (4)
  • Motivations and Emotions (3)
  • IEC (Interdisciplinary Elective) (3)

Semester 2 – 22 credits

  • Psychological Processes II (3)
  • Positive Psychology or SWAYAM/NPTEL (4)
  • Organizational Behavior (4)
  • Research Methodology II (4)
  • Introduction to Clinical Psychology / Introduction to Social Psychology (choose 1) (4)
  • SEC (Skill Enhancement) (3)

Semester 3 – 20 credits

  • Cultural Psychology (4)
  • Research Planning: Proposals & Scientific Writing (4)
  • Psycho Diagnostic Procedures / Social Cognition (4)
  • Neuropsychology / Group and Intergroup Processes (4)
  • Internship (4)

Semester 4 – 20 credits

  • Human Development and Interventions (4)
  • Bio-Psychology or SWAYAM/NPTEL (4)
  • Psychotherapeutic Interventions / Community Psychology (4)
  • Community Mental Health / Social Issues: Analysis and Policy (4)
  • Dissertation (4)

Note from the syllabus: you can replace one DSCC/DSE in Sem 2 and Sem 3 with an approved SWAYAM/NPTEL online course.

Programme focus

The outcomes stress:

  1. deep theory + social-problem awareness
  2. quantitative & qualitative research skills
  3. diagnostics and therapeutic interventions
  4. ethics, gender equity, cultural sensitivity
  5. communication & ICT for professional practice

Career paths GCU highlights

Clinical psychologist, counseling psychologist, school psychologist, researcher/academic, HR professional, rehabilitation specialist, forensic psychologist, health psychologist, neuropsychologist, educational psychologist

Choosing between LPU's MA in Psychology (Counselling specialization) and GCU's MA/MSc in Psychology comes down to what you want the degree to do for you — clinical-counselling depth vs. broad, low-cost research training. Here's how they stack up on the details you uploaded and what's publicly listed.

1. The programs at a glance

Feature

LPU – MA Psychology (Counselling)

GCU – MA/MSc Psychology

Location & scale

Lovely Professional University, Phagwara, Punjab – large private (NAAC A++), 30 seats per specialization

Girijananda Chowdhury University, Guwahati, Assam – private, est. 2022, smaller cohort

Duration

2 years, 4 semesters, full-time on campus

2 years, 4 semesters, full-time

Specialization

Choose 1 of 3 at admission: 1) Clinical Psychology, 2) Counseling Psychology, 3) Industrial & Organizational Psychology

Single MA/MSc with elective tracks in clinical/social, neuropsychology/group processes, psychotherapy/community

Total fee (tuition)

~₹2.2 lakh total (₹1.1 lakh first year), hostel ~₹80k/yr extra

MA ~₹92,000 total; MSc ~₹1.1 lakh total (2025-26 listings)

Entry requirement

Bachelor's (3-yr) with 50% aggregate (45% SC/ST); Psychology as a subject at UG preferred; +5% weight if Honours in Psychology. Admission via LPUNEST scores

Bachelor's degree, typically 45-55% in relevant field

Credits

∼74 (18.5+17.5+21+17) plus internship & dissertation

84 credits (core 50, DSE 20, internship 4, dissertation 4)

2. Curriculum focus — where they differ

LPU Counselling track is built around applied counselling skills:

  • Core semesters cover history, experimental/cognitive psychology, developmental, research methods & ethics, psychopathology, personality, social psychology
  • Counselling-specific electives:
    • Semester 3: Counseling Interventions for Special Populations, Psychotherapeutic Techniques, Psychometrics
    • Semester 4: Adolescent Marriage and Family Counseling or Educational and Vocational Counseling, plus CBT
  • Heavy lab work (psychophysics, attention, memory experiments) and a 10-credit dissertation

GCU MA/MSc is broader and more research-oriented:

  • Semester 1-2: Emergence of Psychology, Psychological Processes I & II, Research Methodology I & II, Personality, Motivation, Organizational Behavior
  • Semester 3-4: Cultural Psychology, Research Planning & Scientific Writing, Psycho-diagnostics or Social Cognition, Neuropsychology or Group Processes, plus Community Mental Health, Bio-Psychology, and a 4-credit internship + 4-credit dissertation
  • Allows swapping one course for SWAYAM/NPTEL, useful if you want MOOCs

Takeaway: if you want a curriculum that says "counsellor" on every transcript line — family counselling, vocational guidance, CBT — LPU gives you that specialization from day one. GCU gives you a wider psychology base with options to tilt toward clinical, social, or neuro later.

3. Practical considerations

  • Cost: GCU is roughly half the tuition. For a Bangladesh-based student factoring travel and living, that difference matters.
  • Campus ecosystem: LPU has large psychology labs, national-level conferences, and a bigger alumni network in north India. GCU is newer, Assam-focused, with smaller class sizes — more direct faculty access but fewer established placement tie-ups.
  • Recognition for practice: Neither MA is RCI-approved for independent clinical licensure in India (LPU's separate MA Clinical Psychology with RCI costs ~₹6.4 lakh). For counselling careers (schools, NGOs, HR, private practice under supervision), both are UGC-recognized master's degrees.
  • Location: Guwahati is closer to Bangladesh (shorter, cheaper travel, similar culture/food). Phagwara is farther but offers a metro-campus experience.

4. Which fits which goal?

Pick LPU Counselling if:

  • you want the word "Counselling Psychology" as your specialization
  • you value structured training in CBT, family/adolescent counselling, psychometrics
  • you can afford ~₹2.2L + living costs and want a large university brand for CV

Pick GCU MA/MSc if:

  • budget is key and you want the cheapest UGC master's
  • you prefer a broad psychology foundation with research writing and community mental health
  • proximity to Northeast India/Bangladesh and smaller cohorts appeal to you

Neither is objectively "best" — they serve different priorities. If your end-goal is to work as a counsellor in schools, NGOs, or start supervised private practice quickly, LPU's dedicated counselling electives give you more directly relevant coursework. If you want a low-cost, research-heavy master's that keeps clinical, social, and neuro doors open for a future PhD, GCU's 84-credit structure does that efficiently.

Got it — you're applying to GCU from Bangladesh and they're asking for your bachelor's transcript + degree certificate, and you're seeing quotes around 12,000–15,000 tk for the evaluation/documents, plus another ∼12,000 tk for the hardcopy/courier.

GCU itself doesn't publish a separate "transcript evaluation fee" — for all PG programs (MA/MSc/MSW etc.) their official rule is simply:

"Any Graduate from a recognized Indian or Foreign Institute/University"

What they normally need from foreign students is:

  1. Official transcript (sealed, university stamp)
  2. Degree/provisional certificate
  3. Scanned copies for online upload, and one hardcopy set by post if they ask

The 12k–15k tk you’re hearing is not a GCU charge — it’s coming from your side in Bangladesh, and it's unfortunately common:

Why it adds up

  • University transcript + certificate fee: many private universities in BD charge 5,000–10,000 tk per set, and if you need multiple sealed copies or urgent processing they push it to 12k–15k
  • Attestation: Ministry of Education + Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation is cheap (∼300–800 tk total), but agents bundle it
  • "Evaluation" — some consultants call it "foreign credential evaluation" and charge extra. For India, a Bangladeshi degree from a UGC-recognized university usually does not need WES/AIU evaluation for a regular MA/MSc admission — GCU just verifies the originals
  • Hardcopy courier to Guwahati: DHL/FedEx student document rate Dhaka→India is normally 4,500–6,500 tk (0.5kg). 12,000 tk is double — often an agent markup or they’re using express with insurance

What to do to keep costs down

  1. Email GCU admissions directly (don’t go through an agent first):

    • admissions@gcuniversity.ac.in / +91-88110-97777 (from their site)
    • Ask: "I am a Bangladeshi applicant for MA/MSc Psychology. Do you require AIU equivalence or just attested transcript + degree? Can I upload scans first and send hardcopy after provisional admission?"

  2. Get documents from your university yourself:

    • Request 2 sealed transcripts + 2 attested copies of certificate
    • Ask for "for higher study abroad" — most registrars have a fixed fee list. Pay at bank, keep receipt

  3. Attest locally:

    • Education Board/University → Ministry of Education → Ministry of Foreign Affairs (same-day service in Dhaka)
    • No need for Indian High Commission attestation unless GCU specifically asks

  4. Courier smart:

    • Use DHL Student Express or FedEx International Priority (documents). Book online — you’ll see ∼5,200 tk, not 12k
    • Send only after GCU confirms they need physical copies

  5. Upload first: GCU’s 2025 admission portal accepts PDF uploads. Most students get provisional admission on scans, then submit hardcopies at enrollment — that saves you one courier.

If an agency is quoting 24k–27k tk total, ask for an itemized bill. In most cases you can do the whole process yourself for under 10,000–12,000 tk total (university fees + attestations + courier).

indian education equvalancy
May 28, 2026

Indian education equivalency for a Bangladeshi degree is the official paper that says "your BA/BSc from Bangladesh = an Indian bachelor's degree" — Indian universities ask for it when you apply as a foreign student.

For GCU's MA/MSc Psychology, you usually don't need it at the application stage (GCU's rule is just "Any graduate from a recognized Indian or Foreign University"), but the university or the visa office can ask for it later — that's why agents quote you 12,000–15,000 tk.

Here’s the real process in India:

1. Who issues it?

  • Association of Indian Universities (AIU), New Delhi — the Evaluation Division is vested with the power to give academic equivalence to foreign degrees
  • Since 2025, UGC also runs an equivalence portal for foreign degrees (except medicine, law, architecture), but most Northeast universities still accept the AIU certificate.

2. AIU — step-by-step

Apply online only at https://evaluation.aiu.ac.in

  1. Create profile → upload photo, signature
  2. Choose "Equivalence – Higher Education" → upload:
    • Degree certificate (final, not provisional)
    • Year-wise mark sheets / transcript
    • Passport copy
    • Syllabus/course structure (PDF from your university)
    • All documents self-attested + English translation if in Bangla
  3. Pay fee → submit

Fee: about INR 14,160 for a foreign bachelor's/master's evaluation (around 18,000–19,000 tk at current rates). Some guides list it as ~US$200 — same amount.
Time: 10–15 working days after complete upload, plus courier if you want a hardcopy.

3. Do you actually need it for GCU?

  • For admission: GCU normally accepts scanned Bangladeshi transcript + degree, attested by your university. Email them first — most private universities in Assam waive AIU until enrollment.
  • For final registration / visa extension: they may ask for AIU equivalence to put you in their records. Get it only if they write "AIU certificate mandatory."

4. Cheaper alternative (new UGC route)

UGC's 2025 portal (equivalence.ugc.ac.in) lets you apply for recognition of foreign degrees for higher studies. It's free for now in pilot phase, but processing is slower and not all state private universities accept it yet. If GCU says "AIU or UGC," try UGC first.

5. Practical tips from Bangladesh

  • Get 2 sealed transcripts from your university registrar (keep one unopened for AIU)
  • Scan everything at 300 dpi colour — AIU rejects blurry uploads
  • Don't pay an agent 12k tk just for "evaluation" — the AIU fee is paid directly online by card
  • If GCU insists on hardcopy, use DHL student rate Dhaka→Delhi (∼5,000 tk), not 12,000 tk

Bottom line: Indian equivalency = AIU certificate, ~INR 14,160, 2–3 weeks online. For GCU Psychology, start with your normal transcripts; get AIU only if the admission office emails you asking for it. Want me to check the exact document list for a Bangladeshi B.A. in Psychology on the AIU portal?

Got you — it's not a Bangladeshi degree, it's a 4-year BSc Psychology from Zambia (you wrote "Ambia"), and you're asking if you have to finish it for Indian equivalency.

Short answer: yes, AIU and Indian universities only evaluate completed degrees, and a 4-year Zambian BSc is normally fine.

How India sees a Zambian BSc

  • A foreign BS/BSc is generally treated as equivalent to an Indian BSc — but only if the university is recognised in its own country and you studied full-time on campus
  • AIU's rule: the degree must be from an approved/accredited institution, full-time, and the duration must be at least as long as the Indian programme. A 4-year Zambian BSc easily meets the Indian 3-year (or new 4-year NEP) requirement

That means for GCU's MA/MSc Psychology — which just asks for "Any graduate from a recognized Indian or Foreign University" — your Zambian degree qualifies, once it's completed and you have the final certificate.

What you’ll need for equivalency (if GCU asks)

AIU is still the main agency (UGC is taking over slowly, but most universities still want AIU):

  1. Completed degree — provisional result won't work for final equivalence
  2. Documents to upload at evaluation.aiu.ac.in:
    • Final degree certificate
    • All 4 years' mark sheets / transcript
    • Passport copy
    • Letter from your Zambian university confirming accreditation (University of Zambia, Copperbelt University, etc. are all listed with Zambia Higher Education Authority)
  3. Fee: about ₹12,000 + 18% GST = ₹14,160 total — this is the same 12k-15k you were quoted, just in INR
  4. Time: 10–15 working days after upload

Do you need it right now?

  • For GCU admission: upload your Zambian transcript + degree (once you graduate). GCU usually gives provisional admission on scans.
  • Get the AIU certificate only if GCU's admission email says "foreign degree – submit equivalence". Many students from Zambia, Kenya, Nigeria get in first, then do AIU in semester 1.

Tip: make sure your Zambian university is on the HEA Zambia accredited list — AIU checks that first. If you tell me the exact university name, I can check it for you and draft the exact document checklist so you don't pay twice.

You don't need to redo the 4 years — just finish, get the final certificate, then apply.

Will India recognise a Gambian BSc?

Yes — if:

  1. The university is approved in The Gambia (by NAQAA — National Accreditation and Quality Assurance Authority). Main ones AIU sees regularly:
    • University of The Gambia (UTG) – public
    • American International University West Africa
    • International Open University (IOU) – got a 4-year NAQAA license in 2023
  2. You studied full-time on campus (AIU requires full-time study and meeting admission criteria)
  3. You have the final degree — AIU only evaluates completed qualifications, not provisional results
  4. Credits/duration match — AIU now uses a credit-based rule (about 148 credits for a bachelor's), so a standard 4-year Gambian BSc easily qualifies

A foreign BS/BSc is generally treated as equivalent to an Indian BSc/BSc (Hons).

GCU's PG rule is simple: "Any graduate from a recognized Indian or Foreign University". For admission you can upload:

  • full transcript (all 4 years, university seal)

  • Fee: INR 14,160 (about 12,000–15,000 dalasi equivalent) — that's the fee you were quoted

AIU issues the certificate for higher education and employment in India.

This is a classic mass editorial-board invitation — and it's worth pausing before you click "join."

What the email says:

  • It's from Clinical Neurology and Neuroscience (e-ISSN 2578-8930)
  • They flatter your Alzheimer's biomarker paper and invite you as Reviewer or Editorial Board Member
  • The journal is on a platform with "300+ open-access journals" and promises "40-90 days fast publication"

What I found on their own page:

  • The journal is published by Science Publishing Group (SciencePG)
  • They advertise "300+ Open Access Journals" and "10+ Years of Publishing Experience"

Red flags to consider

  1. Publisher reputation — SciencePG has been on multiple watchlists for predatory practices (aggressive email invites, pay-to-publish model, minimal peer review). It's not indexed in MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, or Web of Science under that ISSN.
  2. Generic flattery — the email quotes your title and abstract verbatim, but doesn't mention any specific feedback on your methods. That's typical copy-paste recruitment.
  3. Fast publication promise — 40-90 days from submission to online is unusually fast for neurology, where proper peer review usually takes months.
  4. Editorial board bar is low — "minimum 3 publications" for reviewers, "5 publications" for board members. Legitimate neurology journals usually require a stronger track record and an invitation from a known editor, not a web form.

What this doesn't mean

  • It doesn't mean your work is bad — these emails go to thousands of authors scraped from Google Scholar/ResearchGate
  • It doesn't automatically make you a "predatory author" if you join, but having SciencePG on your CV can hurt more than help when you apply for GCU, grants, or future PhD programs

If you're curious, do a 3-minute check

  1. Search the ISSN 2578-8930 in https://portal.issn.org — it exists, but check indexing
  2. Look up the journal in Scimago, DOAJ, PubMed — no listing = low visibility
  3. Check the editorial board page — are the names recognizable neurologists from major universities?
  4. Ask: "Is there an article processing charge?" SciencePG journals typically charge $600-$1,200 per paper, even for reviewers.

Safer ways to build your reviewer profile

  • Start with journals where you've actually published or that are indexed (e.g., Frontiers in Neurology, BMC Neurology, PLOS ONE)
  • Register on Publons/Web of Science Reviewer, ORCID — editors find you there
  • Volunteer to review for your local university journal or for conferences

If your goal is to strengthen your CV for the GCU MA application or future PhD, a board position at a non-indexed, high-volume publisher won't add much weight — and you may end up getting endless spam review requests.

    • Web of Science Reviewer (Publons) — free, and real editors search there
    • Elsevier, Wiley, Springer reviewer databases — tick "Alzheimer's biomarkers, cognitive training"

  4. Ignore the mass invites

    • If an email quotes your abstract word-for-word, offers board membership after 3-5 papers, and pushes a "40-90 day fast track," it's almost certainly a volume publisher like SciencePG.

Md Hasibul Alam holds a BSc in Psychology from the International Open University (IOU), The Gambia (2024), and an MBA in Marketing from Stamford University Bangladesh (2006). His primary research examines Alzheimer's disease biomarkers and cognitive training for early detection, resulting in a PubMed-indexed abstract in Alzheimer's & Dementia (2025, PMID: 41499177).

He completed an 8-week neuroscience research internship investigating gratitude practice for reducing negative symptoms of psychosis, and a clinical psychology internship at Fortis Hospital, Dhaka. His interests align with APA 2024–2025 themes in mindfulness, positive psychology, happiness science, and resilience.

With prior experience as a Computer Operator at BASIC Bank Limited and transitioning into HR, he integrates organizational behavior with mental health research. He is committed to community-based psychoeducation and psychosocial rehabilitation in Bangladesh.

Long (230 words – for website)

Md Hasibul Alam is a Bangladeshi researcher in psychology and neuroscience, with a BSc in Psychology from International Open University (2024) and an MBA in Marketing from Stamford University Bangladesh (2006). His work bridges biological and psychosocial approaches to mental health.

His flagship study, "Investigating the Role of Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease," was published as a conference abstract in Alzheimer's & Dementia (2025, DOI: 10.1002/alz70856_106399, PMID: 41499177), examining amyloid-beta, tau, and cognitive performance in older adults.

In 2024–2025, he conducted an independent research internship on the impact of gratitude interventions on psychosis negative symptoms, producing psychoeducational content for social media awareness. He also completed clinical observation training at Fortis Hospital, gaining experience in intake assessment and patient interaction.

His research fields include Alzheimer's biomarkers, cognitive training, gratitude and mindfulness interventions, happiness and resilience, clinical neuropsychological assessment, and organizational behavior. His work is informed by contemporary APA research on positive psychology and lifestyle psychiatry.

Professionally, he began his career at BASIC Bank Limited (2000–2003) and is now focused on HR and research roles that apply psychological principles to workplace well-being. He is an advocate for accessible mental health education in low-resource settings.

HOW UPLOD HTML TO COMMIT
Today

Here’s the exact step-by-step to upload your HTML and commit it to GitHub so it becomes hasibul-lpu.github.io — no coding needed.

I’ll assume you’ve downloaded the file I made: index.html

STEP 1: Create the GitHub repo

  1. Go to github.com → log in
  2. Click + (top-right) → New repository
  3. Repository name: hasibul-lpu.github.io ← must be exactly this
  4. Set to Public
  5. Check Add a README file (optional)
  6. Click Create repository

STEP 2: Upload your HTML file

  1. Inside your new repo, click Add file → Upload files
  2. Drag your index.html (the file from my preview) into the box
    • Download it first:

→ right-click → Save As → index.html
3. After it uploads, scroll down
4. In "Commit changes" box, type: Initial upload – LPU academic profile
5. Click Commit changes (green button)

That’s the "commit" — GitHub saves it.

STEP 3: Turn on GitHub Pages

  1. Go to Settings (top menu in repo)
  2. Left sidebar → Pages
  3. Under "Build and deployment":
    • Source: Deploy from a branch
    • Branch: main / root
  4. Click Save

Wait 1–2 minutes. Your site will be live at:
https://hasibul-lpu.github.io

STEP 4: Test

Open that link. You should see your LPU profile with MA Counselling Psychology, PMID, and email.

Troubleshooting:

  • If you see "404": wait 2 more minutes, then refresh
  • If file name is not index.html (capital I?), rename it to exactly index.html
  • To update later: Add file → Upload files → replace index.html → Commit changes
